title: Necessity and Sufficiency
coreMove: Separate must-have conditions from enough-to-produce conditions before choosing the lever.
sourcePressure: Frozen support is thin and limited to the chapter identity plus the safe distinction between conditions that must be present and conditions that are enough to produce an outcome. Do not import formal logic history or named authorities.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version treats every useful factor as necessary or assumes one missing ingredient explains the whole outcome.

sourceAnchors.name: Necessity and Sufficiency
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen bundle confirms only the chapter/supporting idea title and a narrow factual floor for must-be-present versus enough-to-produce conditions
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The useful distinction is small enough to hold in one hand: some things must be there, and some things are enough to make the result happen.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: a clinic nurse helping a patient identify what produces hives
exampleSpecs.stakes: the patient may cut foods randomly while missing the sufficient trigger combination
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Emma separates foods that were present during every reaction from the one food-medication combination that is enough to reproduce the rash
exampleSpecs.firstImage: red welts circled in pen on an allergy diary page

exampleSpecs.audience: a port coordinator trying to restart a delayed dredging project
exampleSpecs.stakes: the crew may chase optional paperwork while the missing permit blocks everything
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Louis sorts the checklist into must-be-present approvals and enough-to-start approvals before calling another contractor
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a tide chart taped beside a stack of unsigned permits

exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer coordinator assembling a weekend tournament
exampleSpecs.stakes: games cannot start if one required referee condition is absent
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Nina asks which conditions are nice, which are required, and which set is enough to begin the first match safely
exampleSpecs.firstImage: orange corner flags bundled beside an empty referee sign-in table

exampleSpecs.audience: a head brewer diagnosing a sour batch
exampleSpecs.stakes: another ruined batch will waste tanks during a seasonal release
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hiroshi marks sanitation as necessary for good beer but not sufficient, then finds the temperature spike that is enough to explain this fault
exampleSpecs.firstImage: condensation streaking down a stainless fermenter

exampleSpecs.audience: a garden board deciding why seedlings keep dying
exampleSpecs.stakes: volunteers may keep adding mulch when water pressure is the missing condition
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Maja names sunlight and soil as necessary but shows the dry pressure gauge that prevents either from being enough
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a cracked pressure gauge zip-tied to a raised bed

exampleSpecs.audience: a clinic intake lead designing criteria for eviction help
exampleSpecs.stakes: eligible tenants could be turned away because helpful signals are confused with required ones
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Luca move income, notice date, county, and hearing date into necessary or sufficient groups before training volunteers
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stamped eviction notice half-covered by intake sticky notes

skillTargets: avoid treating helpful factors as required
choose the condition that actually produces the outcome

tryThisNowSpec: For one desired outcome, write two lines: what must be present, and what would be enough to make it happen. Cross out anything merely helpful.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
